claims.claim: That page reports the guideline establishes a near-blanket ban on using LLMs to generate or rewrite article content.
claims.quote: the use of LLMs to generate or rewrite article content is prohibited

claims.claim: That page states LLM outputs become worse when the questions are complicated or about obscure subjects.
claims.quote: outputs become worse when they are asked questions that are complicated

claims.claim: Min and colleagues human-evaluated the factual precision of people biographies generated by commercial language models and found ChatGPT reached only 58%.
claims.source: Sewon Min et al., 'FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation', arXiv:2305.14251

claims.claim: Their reported FActScores on people biographies are 42.5% for InstructGPT, 58.3% for ChatGPT and 71.5% for the retrieval-augmented PerplexityAI.
claims.source: Sewon Min et al., arXiv:2305.14251, Table 1
claims.quote: FACT S COREs of 42.5% and 58.3%, respectively.

claims.claim: They find factual precision falls as the subject person becomes rarer in the pretraining corpora, consistently across all the models tested.
claims.quote: Error rates are higher for rarer entities.

verdicts.note: Raw wikitext via ?action=raw. § Usage/Writing articles: the guideline on writing articles using LLMs 'establishes a near-blanket ban', and the claim's quote appears word for word in that same sentence. Exceptions named on the page (translation, basic copyediting) are consistent with 'near-blanket'. The page itself is an information page reporting on the separate guideline, which is exactly what the claim asserts.

verdicts.trueWording: "outputs become worse ... complicated, about obscure subjects" — § Risks
verdicts.note: Raw wikitext. Sentence reads: LLMs' outputs become worse when they are asked questions that are complicated, about obscure subjects, or told to do tasks to which they are not suited. Claim's quote is verbatim; both limbs (complicated, obscure) supported. Locator note: the heading is '== Risks ==' carrying the anchor id 'Risks and relevant policies', so the claim's section pointer resolves.

arXiv abstract HTML fetched and the blockquote extracted raw. Quote appears verbatim in parentheses. Every limb supported by the same abstract: 'We conduct an extensive human evaluation to obtain FACTSCOREs of people biographies generated by several state-of-the-art commercial LMs'; the title supplies 'factual precision'.

PDF fetched as binary and text-extracted with pdftotext. §3.4: InstructGPT and ChatGPT achieve FACTSCOREs of 42.5% and 58.3%, respectively; PerplexityAI attains 71.5%. Table 1's FACTSCORE row reads 42.5 / 58.3 / 71.5. The spacing in the claim's quote ('FACT S CORE') is a small-caps extraction artifact, not a mismatch; 'retrieval-augmented PerplexityAI' is the abstract's own phrase.

verdicts.trueWording: "Error rates are higher for rarer entities" — §3.4 subheading
verdicts.note: Verbatim §3.4 run-in heading. Supporting text: 'a notable decrease in FACTSCORE as the rarity of entities increases, consistently across all LMSUBJs', over 'frequency levels of topic entities (humans) in the pretraining corpora'. All three limbs (falls with rarity, pretraining corpora, consistent across models) supported.

verdicts.trueWording: "higher for facts mentioned later in the generation" — §3.4
verdicts.note: Verbatim contiguous prefix of the §3.4 run-in heading 'Error rates are higher for facts mentioned later in the generation.' Supporting text: 'Across all LMs, the later part of the generation has significantly worse precision', measured over relative positions (Figure 2, bottom); the generations are the people biographies of §3.3.

verdicts.trueWording: "Wrong date, wrong year, wrong city" — birth-date passage
verdicts.note: Slate live page fetched with a browser user agent; article body extracted raw. The obituary states he was born Dec. 27, 1966, in Cincinnati, followed parenthetically by the quote verbatim. Same paragraph attributes the obituary to Davinci-003.

verdicts.trueWording: "this has no basis in reality" — education passage
verdicts.note: Raw body: the program said he 'went on to earn a Ph.D. in mathematics from Berkeley (this has no basis in reality)'. Quote verbatim; the 'never held' limb is exactly what the parenthetical asserts.

Raw body: he says he did not write From E=mc2 to Schrodinger's Cat, followed by '(As far as I can tell, no such book exists.)' — the claim's quote verbatim. The obituary had credited him with that title.

verdicts.trueWording: "subjects from the wrong department" — NYU courses sentence
verdicts.note: Raw body: 'It listed the names of courses I taught at NYU—all not just wrong, but subjects from the wrong department.' Quote verbatim; both limbs (courses he taught, wrong university department) supported.

verdicts.trueWording: "my legacy was transformed into a cliché" — opening section
verdicts.note: Raw body, second paragraph: 'I was even amused by the way my legacy was transformed into a cliché', followed by the obituary's 'fondly remembered ... for his wit, intelligence, and enthusiasm for life'. Quote verbatim. Note of register, not a grade change: he names it as something the obituary did but explicitly as a thing he was amused by rather than disturbed by — the claim asserts only the former.

verdicts.trueWording: "no such obituary ever existed" — sourcing experiment
verdicts.note: Raw body: he asked the model to indicate and cite an external source for each sentence; it said his Berkeley education came from his New York Times obituary, cited with a URL that looked like it came from the Times website, then 'Of course, no such obituary ever existed.' All four limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: "BS references to back up its BS facts" — sourcing experiment
verdicts.note: Raw body, closing sentence of the sourcing paragraph: 'The A.I. was making up BS references to back up its BS facts.' Quote verbatim; it is the author's own summing-up of that experiment, as the claim says.

verdicts.trueWording: "believable facsimile ... every bit as deep" — closing section
verdicts.note: Raw body, final paragraph: 'The implicit effort that's put in to create a believable facsimile of a source is every bit as deep as the effort to generate an answer in the first place.' The claim's quote is a verbatim contiguous prefix; the 'as deep as generating the answer' limb is the rest of the same sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: "both references are entirely made up" — plagiarism experiment
verdicts.note: Raw body: on a purely non-creative task (detecting plagiarism), given a passage he had written about the NSA, the model flagged one sentence as from an ACLU webpage and another as from Wired, then 'but both references are entirely made up.' Every limb supported.
